subject: Conversation handoff delay: NovusPay live chat slowdown
messages:
From: Grace Huang <grace@novuspay.com>
To: maya_srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>; NovusPay Support <support@novuspay.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Nov 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Live chat responses stalling intermittently (NovusPay)

Hey Maya / Redwood team,

We started seeing our live-chat widget intermittently pause mid-response this morning. Users report the assistant stops streaming for 4–8s and then continues; in some cases it never completes and we see a connection error. This is notably showing up during peak, ~11:00–12:00 PT.

We've attached a small sample of connection logs and a client trace. Can your team advise fast mitigations? This is impacting our checkout assistance flows.

Thanks,
Grace Huang
Sr. Product Manager, NovusPay

Attachment: novuspay-connection-logs-1105.txt (text)

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
To: Grace Huang <grace@novuspay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Nov 2027 16:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Live chat responses stalling intermittently (NovusPay)

Hi Grace — thank you for the report and the logs. We're looking into telemetry now. Initial hypothesis: sporadic backpressure on streaming paths in the us-west edge pool during the peak window.

Short-term we can recommend a couple of quick mitigations so you can keep the widget usable while we triage:
- Switch to non-streaming responses for checkout flows (add ?stream=false or set streaming=false in your SDK call) — this avoids partial-stream stalls at the cost of slightly higher end-to-end latency.
- Reduce max_tokens to 256 for checkout assistant requests and increase client read timeout to 20s.
- If you rely on streaming for progressive UI, enable client-side chunk timeout/backoff: retry the request once with exponential backoff (200ms -> 600ms) and resume.

I'll loop in operations and escalate if we see systemic issues. Ben / Laura — can you confirm if there were any autoscaling events or known edge saturations for us-west around 11:00–12:00 PT?

Maya
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 06 Nov 2027 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Live chat responses stalling intermittently (NovusPay)

Maya / team — we pulled the edge and serving telemetry. Summary: between 10:40–12:10 PT on 2027-11-05 we saw elevated queueing on the streaming workers that handle the incremental token emit path. Root contributors: a small config change in the HTTP front proxy that increased connection reuse timeouts (longer-lived sockets) combined with a token-burst workload from a partner test bucket. The runtime didn't reclaim hot KV-cache slots fast enough under the increased per-connection cost, which amplified tail latency for streaming emits.

Actions taken (short-term):
- Rolled back the front proxy change at 11:28 PT — immediate tail improvement observed.
- Increased the streaming worker autoscale headroom for us-west by +15% for the next 24 hours.

Customer-facing mitigations (we should send these to Grace):
1) For immediate stability: switch affected routes to blocking/non-streaming generation (stream=false) until we confirm steady tail reduction.
2) If you need streaming UX: lower max_tokens, cap concurrent requests per session (<=3), and enable client-side chunk-retries as Maya recommended.
3) We can provision a temporary dedicated capacity slot (small dedicated pool) for NovusPay for the weekend — if they want guaranteed throughput.

I'll prepare a short internal incident note and coordinate a formal postmortem.
-Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: rl_trace_excerpt_1106.json (truncated trace)

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
To: Grace Huang <grace@novuspay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 07 Nov 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Action plan and immediate workarounds — NovusPay live chat

Hi Grace — short update and clear next steps from our side. Thanks again for the logs; they were helpful. TL;DR: we identified a transient configuration change that increased streaming tail latency and rolled it back. We recommend the following while we complete validation and monitoring: 

Your immediate options (pick one based on UX tolerance):
- Option A (lowest user disruption): switch the checkout assistant calls to non-streaming (stream=false). We can provide a 1-click SDK patch you can drop-in; ETA 1 hour for our devs to validate with your staging token.
- Option B (keep streaming with safeguards): keep streaming enabled but set max_tokens=250, limit concurrency per session to 2 requests, and add a simple client-side retry with 300ms initial backoff. This will reduce the incidence of stalls.
- Option C (guaranteed): accept a temporary dedicated capacity slot for the next 48–72 hours; we'll size it to your peak and provide an SLA window. This requires a quick procurement sign-off.

What we'll do now:
- Ben and Karthik will run a telemetry baseline sweep through Monday and provide sustained tail-latency numbers.
- I'll schedule a 30-minute postmortem sync with your ops team on Monday (Nov 8) to review findings and remediation timeline.
- If you choose Option C, I'll put you in touch with our Sales Ops to generate a short-term commitment.

If you want, we can do the SDK patch for Option A now and roll it to staging; tell me which route you prefer and I'll coordinate.

Best,
Maya
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
